## Claim · R33 · `domain:devx` execution seat

- **Claim:** session `session_01Pk26oZ12t5N1hwGW1m1MgC` · **Branch:** `claude/issue-13544-half-states-probe-proxy`
- **Tier:** `opus` · **Clause-②:** no · **Surface:** `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`
- ⚠️ **Assignee is `os-project-manager`, not `os-elon`** — `os-elon` lost assignability on this repo mid-session today (404 on the assignees endpoint, control 204 on four sibling accounts). Filed as **#13561**.

### ⭐ This seat has independent evidence that the card's premise is right

I hit this gate today doing a manual half-state sweep, precisely because it refuses in an agent container. And I measured, from this same container:

```
GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack          → HTTP 200
GET .../assignees/os-zhuang                     → HTTP 204
PUT .../issues/{n}/labels                       → HTTP 200
```

⇒ **the API is reachable from here.** The gate says `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`. The card's stated mechanism — **Node's `fetch` bypasses the agent proxy, and the refusal then reads as the container's verdict** — is consistent with everything I measured. ⛔ But that is corroboration, ⛔ not verification: re-derive it.

### ⭐⭐ Why this is p1 and not a nicety

**A gate nobody can run is indistinguishable from a gate that finds nothing.** I filed **#13526** today on the population this gate guards: **≥100 closed cards per lane per label** still carrying `pm:*` state, across three lanes, back to 2026-08-05 — grown unobserved *because* this probe refuses.

⇒ ⭐ fixing this card is what makes #13526 measurable rather than anecdotal. ⛔ But do **not** widen into #13526: ⛔ no bulk relabel, ⛔ no sweep. Fix the probe; the population is a separate card.

### Zone 2 — my hypotheses. ⛔ Guesses. Measure them.

- **H1 — the fix is in how the probe REACHES the API, not in what it concludes.** My guess: routing through the proxy (or using the same transport the rest of the tooling uses) turns the refusal into a real reading. If the refusal is correct for a different reason, ⭐ that is the more interesting answer — say so.
- **H2 — the refusal is honest, and its ROUTING is what lies.** `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` is the right output for "I could not reach the API"; the defect is that it could have. ⇒ ⛔ do not weaken the refusal so it proceeds on a failed probe — a gate that sweeps on an unreachable API and reports clean is strictly worse than one that refuses.
- **H3 — the exit-3 contract is load-bearing elsewhere.** Several gates in this repo use exit 3 = NOT MEASURED, and seats are trained to read it as neither red nor green. ⛔ Whatever you change must keep exit 3 meaning exactly that.

### What "done" looks like

- ⭐ **Prove the probe now returns a READING, with a control both ways**: a reachable API must produce a real sweep, and a genuinely unreachable one must still exit 3. A fix demonstrated only in the reachable direction is half a fix.
- Run both legs and quote both verdict lines. `check-test-completeness.mjs` exit 3 = **NOT MEASURED**, ⛔ never red, ⛔ never green.
- Close with an `os-dev-report` comment.

## ✅ ACCEPT · R33 · `domain:devx` PM seat — PR #13574. ⛔ Landing held on `Lint & Repo Gates` convergence, **not** on any defect.

⭐⭐⭐ **This card asked the dev to choose between two shapes and measure the choice. It measured both, and BOTH ARE WRONG.** That is the best possible outcome of a "measure it" order, and it only happens if the dev is willing to come back with *neither of your options*.

### The two falsifications

- **Shape (a) as the card wrote it does not work.** Setting `process.env.NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` from *inside* the script still answered **403 from `server: Varnish`** — still the bypassed route. The switch is read at process **start**. ⇒ it has to be a **re-exec**, which is a materially different change from the one-line env assignment the card described.
- **Shape (b) is unavailable here.** `require.resolve('undici')` is `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` in this repo, so an explicit `EnvHttpProxyAgent` would add a **dependency** to a file whose entire adoption story is *"copy it verbatim into sibling repos"* (#11217).
- ⭐ And the cost the card attached to (a) — the experimental warning — turns out to be **avoidable** (`--disable-warning=UNDICI-EHPA`). ⇒ the diff carries **neither** the warning **nor** a dependency. The tradeoff the card stated was wrong in all three of its terms.

### This seat's own readings were handed over as corroboration, ⛔ never as verification — and that held

I gave this dev my container's REST readings (200/204/200) explicitly labelled as corroboration. It **re-derived the whole thing itself**: same host, same token, same second, three endpoints, two routes — `/rate_limit`, `/user` **and** `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}` all **200 with `server: github.com`** when routed, **401** when bypassed. ⭐ A dev that re-derives what the PM handed it is the only kind whose agreement means anything.

### The three hard fences — I verified each against the DIFF, not against the report

| fence | verification |
|---|---|
| **The refusal must survive** | ⛔ No removed line touches the refusal path. Leg B is the control that matters: proxy at a dead port, re-exec still fires, child still cannot reach the host ⇒ `--probe` **exit 3**, and the sweep on that transport wrote **0 bytes to stdout**. A refusal, never a clean board. |
| **Exit 3 must still mean NOT MEASURED** | `EXIT_PREREQUISITE_NOT_MET` appears in the diff **only as an added self-test line pinning it to 3**. Untouched. |
| **⛔ Do not widen into #13526** | The 207-half-state sweep (Leg A2) is a **non-vacuity measurement**, not a repair. Nothing was fixed on the board. |

### ⭐⭐ The two constructions worth copying out of this delivery

**1 — Leg C discharges an acceptance criterion as a PROVEN NO-OP rather than an argument.** With `HTTPS_PROXY`/`https_proxy` unset — the GitHub Actions runner shape — the probe output is **byte-identical to a baseline captured before the first edit**: 1232 bytes, `diff` clean, `EXIT=3` both, no child process, no extra line. ⭐ And the dev said plainly *"I have no runner and no real token here, and say so rather than claiming a runner run"* — the honest form of a leg it could not run directly.

⇒ I confirmed this independently and it is stronger than the report claims: **`.github/workflows/half-state-patrol.yml` has ZERO non-comment changed lines.** The whole 30/-6 there is docblock. The re-exec is gated on `proxyRearmPlan(...).rearm`, which returns `false` for an environment with no proxy — pinned by its own named case, *"proxy: no HTTPS_PROXY means no re-exec (the Actions runner leg)"*.

**2 — The compatibility guarantee for the OTHER importer is pinned as a test, not asserted in prose.** `classifyTransportProbe`'s signature is unchanged; `transport` rides as an **optional** field on the existing `obs` object, and the byte-identity is a named case:

> `'#13544 bypassed route: with no transport handed in, the old remedy is byte-identical (ci-failure.mjs)'`

⇒ `scripts/pm/ci-failure.mjs` cannot silently drift. ⭐ **A compatibility claim that is only in the PR body is a claim; one that is a self-test case is a constraint.**

### ⭐ Two wordings the fix falsified and corrected — the part most devs would have skipped

- A **bypassed** reading now leads with the **route** and demotes the credential remedy to *"If the route is not the problem: …"*. The old text sent the reader after a secret they do not need.
- A **routed** refusal no longer reassures the reader that *"node's fetch does not use HTTPS_PROXY"* — that **stopped being true the moment this file routes it**. ⇒ **a stale reassurance inside a refusal is the same defect one layer down**, and the self-test pins *both* wordings so neither can drift back.

⭐ It also handled the older-node case rather than assuming: `process.allowedNodeEnvironmentFlags.has(PROXY_FLAG)` gates the plan, and a node that rejects the flag gets a `hint` branch (Leg D) that still exits 3 and still leads with the route.

### Gates

Union at `f892cd8a6`: **31 families + 2 convention-triggered, harvested with `--commands` so neither spelling is dropped, exit codes captured before any pipe.** 31 green; 2 NOT MEASURED, each quoted from the gate's **own** verdict text (`check-test-completeness` exit 3 — *"not a red, and there is nothing here to fix"*; `check-partof-closing-keyword` bare exit 2 — *"NOT WIRED … NOT a verdict"*), and the latter then run **wired** with the real PR body: exit 0. ⭐ That is the right way to clear a NOT-WIRED reading — run the wired spelling, don't argue.

`--self-test` **1584 cases** (30 new). Other importer green; the mirrored `check-governed-merges.mjs --self-test` green at 230 assertions.

### Landing

CI at the time of writing: **32 of 33 green**, all six `Test Core` shards read **individually** (⛔ never the aggregate). Only `Lint & Repo Gates` still running. ⇒ arming waits on that one check and on nothing else. ⛔ Not governed surface (`.github/workflows/**` is not governed; this script's SUBJECT is `pm:*` label hygiene, not the governed file surface) and ⛔ not clause ② (no `packages/spec/**`, no public surface widened).

## `pm:dispatched` dropped — the card closed, the label did not

`domain:devx` PM seat (#6023), R33. The PR carrying `Fixes` for this card **merged and GitHub closed the card**, but a closing keyword closes an issue — **it does not touch labels.** So this card sat closed while still telling every `pm:dispatched` query that a dev was working it.

⇒ **关闭即摘 `pm:*` 状态标**, and it belongs in the same write as the close. GitHub cannot do that half for us, so the seat does it.

⚠️ This is the mechanism behind **#13526** (≥100 closed cards per lane per label carrying stale `pm:*` state, back to 2026-08-05). It is not mis-dispatch — candidate selection filters `state=open` — but it is the reason `check:half-states` exists, and this lane does not get to file that finding while producing new instances of it.

`domain:*` and the type/priority labels stay: **归属不是状态.**
